findings: 1. Every single achievement counter on the homepage renders as zero. The 'Company Overview' band is built from six animated odometers and on 14 Sep 2026 all six display 0: 0 GW Annual Solar Module Capacity, 0+ Years of Industry Experience, 0+ Satisfied Customers Worldwide, 0+ Dedicated Employees Workforce, 0+ Countries' Market Presence, and 0 GW Solar Cell Capacity by 2026. The script that should count them up is not firing. The paragraph directly above says 3 GW and 13 years - so the page contradicts itself within one screen, and the contradiction resolves in favour of zero, because numbers in a stat band are what visitors actually read. For a manufacturer whose entire B2B pitch is scale, this is the worst possible failure mode.

2. The domain in the Day-1 record is dead, and the ads may be pointing at it. navitassolar.in does not resolve - the connection fails at the SSL handshake, with no response from either the bare host or the www subdomain. The live property is navitassolar.com. The Google Ads Transparency link in the lead record is built on the dead .in domain, which means any Google activity tracked against it is invisible. Before another rupee is spent, every creative destination, every UTM and every listing needs to be audited for which domain it actually carries.

3. The Day-1 leak is confirmed, and the deeper problem is that the funnel serves neither audience. The stub flags homeowner-targeted ads running alongside C&I keyword bidding. The site makes that worse rather than resolving it: there is no residential path (no PM Surya Ghar page, no kW calculator, no subsidy slabs, no rooftop pricing) and no true B2B path either (no downloadable datasheets or IEC/BIS certificates on the homepage, no distributor or dealer application, no RFQ or bulk-quote form, no MOQ or lead-time information, no project case studies). Every route ends at the same generic 'Contact Us Now' button into a Lead Form. A homeowner cannot buy and a procurement head cannot specify.

4. A 'Solar Cells (Upcoming)' tile links to nothing, in the middle of the company's biggest announcement. In the Core Offerings carousel, the Solar Cells card points at navitassolar.com/# - a dead anchor. This is the single most newsworthy thing about Navitas right now: a Rs.1,500 crore investment announced in June 2026 to enter cell manufacturing with pilot wafer and ingot production, timed to ALMM List-II for cells becoming operational on 1 June 2026, which forces government-backed projects toward domestic cells. Developers are actively searching for who will have Indian cells. Navitas has the answer, has funded it, and links it to a hash.

5. The capacity number changes depending on where you look - including inside the company's own materials. The homepage says 3 GW. The credit-rating summary for Navitas Green Solutions says 2 GW. Inc42's profile still says 500 MW expanding to 1.7 GW. Mercom reports the Ahmedabad plant going to 2.5 GW. Revenue is similarly split: the company told the press about Rs.1,300 crore in FY26, while an unlisted-share research note projects Rs.2,387 crore for the same year. For a business courting institutional buyers, distributors and quite possibly public markets, having four live capacity figures in circulation is a due-diligence problem before it is a marketing one. Pick one, date it, and publish it as the canonical number.

6. The awards wall is the largest element on the page and the least usable. There are roughly twenty award images stacked with no filtering, no dates in the layout, no explanatory text and no ordering - and several are duplicated (the same MSME Excellence award twice, Gold Award June 2022 twice, the Suryacon Youth Leadership award three times). Their filenames are stored with Unicode bold-math characters and some carry a double .jpg.jpg extension, which means alt text is effectively unreadable and the images are invisible to search. Most of the awards are from 2022 and 2023; the strongest and most recent - Solar Module Manufacturer of the Year, Chhattisgarh, January 2026 and Best Solar Product Innovation Award, Global Solar Expo, November 2025 - are buried in the middle of the pile rather than leading it.

7. Speed-to-lead and attribution are both unmanaged. One phone number (+91 70 690 70 990) and one email sit in the header; there is no WhatsApp, no chat, no callback scheduler and no stated response time - for a category where a distributor enquiry or a 500 kW rooftop RFQ is worth lakhs and goes to whoever answers first. With a Lead Form objective and no on-site funnel, there are no mid-funnel events to optimise against: no datasheet download, no product-series view, no EPC enquiry, no distributor-application start. Meta is being handed raw form fills as its only signal, on an estimated Rs.20 lakh a month.
